checks: For the simplex the accepted cap law gives centroid criticality, the normal marginal βS_B and the exact scale of J. At a facet normal the original support is the centered barycentric displacement 1/(d+1) times its normal scaling, and the reflected support is d times that displacement. The mixed volumes are β|B|/d and β|B|, so α=d. Every centroid vertex cap is the corresponding pyramid.

For the cube, symmetry gives exactly half the volume in every through-center halfspace, and a containing cap is at least as large. Off null cut sections each opposite pair partitions the old boundary, yielding β=1/2. Each section has area one and the corresponding support height is 1/2.

The proposed box with sides V/m_i has volume V and facet areas m_i=w_i/2. Thus its area measure is the asserted R. The two support integrals give 1/(2d), and subtracting from the halfcube volume gives (d−1)/(2d). Since 1/(2d)≤1/4 and Γ>1/3, the obstruction is strict including d=2.
